Priya / team — technical notes below:

1) Customer content routing:
- By default, customer request/response content is served and stored in the customer region (we deploy model-serving pods in eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 depending on the customer selection). We do NOT replicate customer content to US regions as part of normal serving.
- Exception: our centralized observability pipeline receives aggregated telemetry and certain anonymized request metadata for SLO/health monitoring. That pipeline is hosted in us-east-1 and is operated by our telemetry vendor (TelemetryCo) — the telemetry events are pseudonymized/hashed and we do not store full customer prompt/response content in that pipeline.
- Edge case: if a customer opts into cross-region failover or uses a Dedicated instance with burst-to-shared policy, model execution may fall back to a compatible variant in another region (e.g., us-east-1) if eu capacity is exhausted; we can contractually lock capacity or provide dedicated pools for customers that require strict geo-fencing.

2) Subprocessors:
- The attached subprocessor list (subprocessor-list.csv) includes logical roles and locations. Short-list: TelemetryCo (US), S3-compatible storage (eu/ie), CRL provider (us), model-binaries CDN (de).

3) Controls:
- All cross-border flows use TLS 1.2+ in transit. At rest, we use AES-256. Customers can bring their own KMS (BYOK) — when enabled, keys are regional and we do not have access to plaintext.
- Retention: default logs retention 30 days; customer-managed retention configurable.

4) Artifacts: infra-dataflow-diagram.png attached. I recommend we offer (a) signed SCCs for the top-3 subprocessors, (b) an option to enable BYOK for Globex, and (c) a note that we can gate failover to non-EU regions behind a contractual clause.

— Vivek
